nodes.name: Rayleigh-faded source-relay channels
nodes.statement: The channel coefficients for the link from $\Source{1}$ and $\Source{2}$ to $\Relay$, respectively denoted as $\h{1}$ and $\h{2}$, follow a Rayleigh distribution, i.e., $\h{1} \sim \CG{0}{\CP{1}}$ and $\h{2} \sim \CG{0}{\CP{2}}$.

nodes.name: Symmetric relaying protocol
nodes.statement: Then we exchange the variable $\frac{t+\eta}{t+\zeta}=\frac{x}{x+1}$ and assume that the relaying protocol is symmetric, i.e., $\snravei{1}=\snravei{2}$, yielding $\eta=0$.
nodes.statement_short: Change of variable plus the symmetry assumption $\bar\gamma_1=\bar\gamma_2$, which forces $\eta=0$.

nodes.name: Exponential-decay path-loss model
nodes.statement: The path loss of each link follows an exponential-decay model: if the distance between the two sources is equal to $d$, then $\CP{0} \propto d^{-\alpha}$ where an exponent of $\alpha=4$ corresponds to a typical non line-of-sight propagation \cite{HTHC:08:VTCSpring}. Here we assume that the $\Source{1}\longrightarrow \Source{2}$ link has unit channel mean power, i.e., $\CP{0}=1$.
nodes.statement_short: Path loss decays as $d^{-\alpha}$ with $\alpha=4$, and the $\mathsf{S}_1\to\mathsf{S}_2$ link is normalized to unit mean power.
nodes.section: 4 Numerical Results

nodes.name: Two-way AF DASTC three-phase transmission protocol
nodes.statement:
The communications of the proposed two-way AF DASTC scheme occur in three phases. In the first phase, both $\Source{1}$ and $\Source{2}$ transmit the first row of Alamouti code \cite{Ala:98:JSAC} to $\Relay$ with the same transmit power per symbol $\Ps$. The received signal at the relay $\Relay$ is given by  egin{align} \y{R} = \h{1} \s{1} + \h{2} \x{1} + 
R \end{align} where $\s{1}= [ { egin{array}{*{20}c}{s_1 } & {s_2 } \ \end{array}}]$ and $\x{1}= [ { egin{array}{*{20}c}{x_1 } & {x_2 } \ \end{array}}]$ are the two first rows of the Alamouti codes generated by $\Source{1}$ and $\Source{2}$, respectively. The channel coefficients for the link from $\Source{1}$ and $\Source{2}$ to $\Relay$, respectively denoted as $\h{1}$ and $\h{2}$, follow a Rayleigh distribution, i.e., $\h{1} \sim \CG{0}{\CP{1}}$ and $\h{2} \sim \CG{0}{\CP{2}}$. The vector $
R$ is the complex additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) with zero mean and variance $N_0$. In the second phase, $\Relay$ amplifies the received signal, i.e., $\y{R}$, with the same power constraint as in the first phase and forwards to $\Source{2}$ while $\Source{1}$ sends the second row of the Alamouti code to $\Source{2}$. The received signal at the source $\Source{2}$, $\y{2}$, is written as  egin{align} \y{2} = \h{2} \Gain \y{R} + \h{0} \s{2} + 
{2} \end{align} where $\Gain$ is the scalar amplifying gain at the relay, $\h{0} \sim \CG{0}{\CP{0}}$ is the channel gain for the link between $\Source{1}$ and $\Source{2}$, $\s{2}= [ { egin{array}{*{20}c}{-s_2^{\ast} } & {s_1^{\ast} } \ \end{array}}]$ is the second row of the Alamouti code, and $
{2}$ is the AWGN vector with zero mean and variance $N_0$. Similarly, in the third phase, $\Relay$ transmit $\Gain \y{R}$ whereas $\Source{2}$ sends the second row of the Alamouti code to $\Source{1}$. The received signal at the source $\Source{1}$, $\y{1}$, is shown as  egin{align} \y{1} = \h{1} \Gain \y{R} + \h{0} \x{2} + 
{1} \end{align} where $\x{2}= [ { egin{array}{*{20}c}{-x_2^{\ast} } & {x_1^{\ast} } \ \end{array}}]$ is the second row of Alamouti code and $
{1}$ is the AWGN vector with zero mean and variance $N_0$.
nodes.statement_short: Three-phase bi-directional relaying: both sources send Alamouti row one to the AF relay, then the relay amplifies-and-forwards while each source sends Alamouti row two directly to the other.

nodes.name: Phase 1 — both sources transmit Alamouti row one to the relay
nodes.statement: In the first phase, both $\Source{1}$ and $\Source{2}$ transmit the first row of Alamouti code \cite{Ala:98:JSAC} to $\Relay$ with the same transmit power per symbol $\Ps$. The received signal at the relay $\Relay$ is given by \begin{align} \y{R} = \h{1} \s{1} + \h{2} \x{1} + \nR \end{align} where $\s{1}= [ {\begin{array}{*{20}c}{s_1 } & {s_2 } \\ \end{array}}]$ and $\x{1}= [ {\begin{array}{*{20}c}{x_1 } & {x_2 } \\ \end{array}}]$ are the two first rows of the Alamouti codes generated by $\Source{1}$ and $\Source{2}$, respectively. The channel coefficients for the link from $\Source{1}$ and $\Source{2}$ to $\Relay$, respectively denoted as $\h{1}$ and $\h{2}$, follow a Rayleigh distribution, i.e., $\h{1} \sim \CG{0}{\CP{1}}$ and $\h{2} \sim \CG{0}{\CP{2}}$. The vector $\nR$ is the complex additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) with zero mean and variance $N_0$.
nodes.statement_short: Both sources simultaneously send the first Alamouti row to the relay, which observes their superposition in Rayleigh fading plus AWGN.
nodes.section: 2 System Model of Distributed Alamouti Space-Time Codes with Two-Way AF Relaying

nodes.name: Phase 2 — relay forwards to $\mathsf{S}_2$ while $\mathsf{S}_1$ sends row two
nodes.statement: In the second phase, $\Relay$ amplifies the received signal, i.e., $\y{R}$, with the same power constraint as in the first phase and forwards to $\Source{2}$ while $\Source{1}$ sends the second row of the Alamouti code to $\Source{2}$. The received signal at the source $\Source{2}$, $\y{2}$, is written as \begin{align} \y{2} = \h{2} \Gain \y{R} + \h{0} \s{2} + \n{2} \end{align} where $\Gain$ is the scalar amplifying gain at the relay, $\h{0} \sim \CG{0}{\CP{0}}$ is the channel gain for the link between $\Source{1}$ and $\Source{2}$, $\s{2}= [ {\begin{array}{*{20}c}{-s_2^{\ast} } & {s_1^{\ast} } \\ \end{array}}]$ is the second row of the Alamouti code, and $\n{2}$ is the AWGN vector with zero mean and variance $N_0$.
nodes.statement_short: The relay amplifies and forwards to $\mathsf{S}_2$ while $\mathsf{S}_1$ transmits the second Alamouti row over the direct link.
nodes.section: 2 System Model of Distributed Alamouti Space-Time Codes with Two-Way AF Relaying

nodes.name: Phase 3 — relay forwards to $\mathsf{S}_1$ while $\mathsf{S}_2$ sends row two
nodes.statement: Similarly, in the third phase, $\Relay$ transmit $\Gain \y{R}$ whereas $\Source{2}$ sends the second row of the Alamouti code to $\Source{1}$. The received signal at the source $\Source{1}$, $\y{1}$, is shown as \begin{align} \y{1} = \h{1} \Gain \y{R} + \h{0} \x{2} + \n{1} \end{align} where $\x{2}= [ {\begin{array}{*{20}c}{-x_2^{\ast} } & {x_1^{\ast} } \\ \end{array}}]$ is the second row of Alamouti code and $\n{1}$ is the AWGN vector with zero mean and variance $N_0$.
nodes.statement_short: Symmetric counterpart of phase 2: the relay forwards to $\mathsf{S}_1$ while $\mathsf{S}_2$ sends its second Alamouti row.
nodes.section: 2 System Model of Distributed Alamouti Space-Time Codes with Two-Way AF Relaying

nodes.name: Received signal at the relay (first phase)
nodes.statement: \begin{align} \y{R} = \h{1} \s{1} + \h{2} \x{1} + \nR \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Relay observation is the sum of both sources' Alamouti rows through their channels plus AWGN.
nodes.section: 2 System Model of Distributed Alamouti Space-Time Codes with Two-Way AF Relaying

nodes.name: Received signal at $\mathsf{S}_2$ (second phase)
nodes.statement: \begin{align} \y{2} = \h{2} \Gain \y{R} + \h{0} \s{2} + \n{2} \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: $\mathsf{S}_2$ receives the amplified relay signal plus the direct-link second Alamouti row from $\mathsf{S}_1$.
nodes.section: 2 System Model of Distributed Alamouti Space-Time Codes with Two-Way AF Relaying

nodes.name: Received signal at $\mathsf{S}_1$ (third phase)
nodes.statement: \begin{align} \y{1} = \h{1} \Gain \y{R} + \h{0} \x{2} + \n{1} \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Mirror of the second-phase model, with $\mathsf{S}_1$ as receiver.
nodes.section: 2 System Model of Distributed Alamouti Space-Time Codes with Two-Way AF Relaying

nodes.name: Relay average power constraint
nodes.statement: \begin{align} \EX{\FN{\Gain \y{R}}^2} = \EX{\FN{\s{i}}^2} =\EX{\FN{\x{i}}^2} \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: The relay's transmitted energy is constrained to equal that of each source's codeword.
nodes.section: 2 System Model of Distributed Alamouti Space-Time Codes with Two-Way AF Relaying

nodes.name: CSI-assisted amplifying gain $G$
nodes.statement: \begin{align} \Gain^2 = \left(|\h{1}|^2+ |\h{2}|^2 + \frac{1}{\snrave}\right)^{-1} \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Exact amplification gain: inverse of the summed instantaneous channel powers plus reciprocal average SNR.
nodes.section: 2 System Model of Distributed Alamouti Space-Time Codes with Two-Way AF Relaying

nodes.name: High-SNR approximation of the amplifying gain
nodes.statement: \begin{align} \Gain^2 \approx \left(|\h{1}|^2+ |\h{2}|^2 \right)^{-1} \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: At large SNR the $1/\bar\gamma$ term is dropped from the gain.
nodes.section: 2 System Model of Distributed Alamouti Space-Time Codes with Two-Way AF Relaying

nodes.name: Equivalent Alamouti MIMO model after self-interference cancellation
nodes.statement: \begin{align} \y{1} &= \hnew \B{X} + \z{1} \\ \y{2} &= \hnew \B{S} + \z{2} \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: After self-interference removal each source sees a virtual two-antenna Alamouti channel $\B{h}$.
nodes.section: 2 System Model of Distributed Alamouti Space-Time Codes with Two-Way AF Relaying

nodes.name: Distribution of the equivalent noise vector $\B{z}_i$
nodes.statement: Here, the new noise vector $\z{i}$, with $i \in \{1,2\}$, is the complex Gaussian vector, i.e., $\z{i} \sim \CGV{2}{\B{0}}{N_0\bigl(1+\left|\h{i}\right|^2\Gain^2\bigr)\B{I}_2}$
nodes.statement_short: The post-cancellation noise stays circularly-symmetric Gaussian with variance inflated by $|h_i|^2G^2$.
nodes.section: 2 System Model of Distributed Alamouti Space-Time Codes with Two-Way AF Relaying

nodes.name: Average sum-rate of the proposed scheme
nodes.statement: \begin{align} \Rsum &= \mathbb{E} \biggl\{ \frac{2}{3}\log_2\det\left(\B{I}_2 + \frac{1}{N_0\left(1+\Gain^2 |\h{2}|^2\right)} \hnew^{\dag}\R{\B{s}}\hnew \right) \nonumber \\ &+ \frac{2}{3}\log_2\det\left(\B{I}_2 + \frac{1}{N_0\left(1+ \Gain^2 |\h{1}|^2\right)} \hnew^{\dag}\R{\B{x}}\hnew \right) \biggr\} \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Ergodic sum-rate as the expectation of two log-det MIMO capacity terms, each pre-scaled by $2/3$ for the three-slot protocol.
nodes.section: 3 Average Sum-Rate of Distributed Alamouti Space-Time Codes with Two-Way AF Relaying

nodes.name: Covariance matrices of the Alamouti Gaussian codewords
nodes.statement: Due to the orthogonality of Alamouti codeword, it is easy to see that $\R{\B{s}} = \EX{\B{S} \B{S}^{\dag}} = 2\Ps \B{I}_2$ and $\R{\B{x}} = \EX{\B{X} \B{X}^{\dag}} = 2\Ps \B{I}_2$.
nodes.statement_short: Orthogonality makes both codeword covariance matrices scalar: $2\mathcal{P}_s\B{I}_2$.
nodes.section: 3 Average Sum-Rate of Distributed Alamouti Space-Time Codes with Two-Way AF Relaying

nodes.name: Average sum-rate after determinant simplification
nodes.statement: \begin{align} &\Rsum = \nonumber \\ & \mathbb{E} \biggl\{ \frac{2}{3}\log_2 \biggl[ \left(1+2\snrave\frac{|\h{1}|^2 |\h{2}|^2+|\h{0}|^2\left(|\h{1}|^2 + |\h{2}|^2\right)}{|\h{1}|^2 + 2|\h{2}|^2}\right) \nonumber \\ &\times \left(1+2\snrave\frac{|\h{1}|^2 |\h{2}|^2+|\h{0}|^2\left(|\h{1}|^2 + |\h{2}|^2\right)}{|\h{2}|^2 + 2|\h{1}|^2}\right) \biggr] \biggr\} \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Scalarized sum-rate: expectation of a $\log_2$ of a product of two SNR-like factors in $|h_0|^2,|h_1|^2,|h_2|^2$.
nodes.section: 3 Average Sum-Rate of Distributed Alamouti Space-Time Codes with Two-Way AF Relaying

nodes.name: Sylvester determinant identity
nodes.statement: where \eqref{eq:SumRate:2} is established by the fact that $\det\left(\B{I} + \B{A} \B{B}\right)=\det\left(\B{I} + \B{B} \B{A}\right)$.
nodes.statement_short: Commuting-product determinant identity used to scalarize the log-det terms.
nodes.section: 3 Average Sum-Rate of Distributed Alamouti Space-Time Codes with Two-Way AF Relaying
nodes.origin_citation: Sylvester's determinant identity (uncited in this paper)

nodes.name: High-SNR decomposition of the sum-rate into $I_1$, $I_2$, $I_3$
nodes.statement: \begin{align} \frac{3 \ln2}{2} \Rsum &\approx \underbrace { \EX{\ln\left(\frac{\snri{1}\snri{2}}{\snri{1}+2\snri{2}}\right)} }_{I_1} + \underbrace { \EX{\ln\left(\frac{\snri{1}\snri{2}}{\snri{2}+2\snri{1}}\right)} }_{I_2} \nonumber \\ &+ 2 \underbrace { \EX{\ln\left(1+\frac{\snri{0}\left(\snri{1}+\snri{2}\right)}{\snri{1}\snri{2}}\right)} }_{I_3} \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: At high SNR the sum-rate splits into three logarithmic expectations $I_1$, $I_2$ and $2I_3$.
nodes.section: 3 Average Sum-Rate of Distributed Alamouti Space-Time Codes with Two-Way AF Relaying

nodes.name: Integral representation of $I_1$
nodes.statement: \begin{align} I_1 = \sum\limits_{u=1}^{2} \sum\limits_{v=0}^{1} \int\limits_{0}^{\infty} \mathcal{A}_v \frac{\ln z}{1+z} z^{u} \exp(-\beta_1 z) \Bessel{v}{ \alpha z} dz \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: $I_1$ written as a double sum of integrals of $\ln z/(1+z)$ against an exponentially weighted Bessel kernel.
nodes.section: 3 Average Sum-Rate of Distributed Alamouti Space-Time Codes with Two-Way AF Relaying

nodes.name: Meijer G-function representations of $\ln z/(1+z)$ and $e^{-\alpha z}\mathcal{K}_v(\alpha z)$
nodes.statement: \begin{align} \frac{\ln z}{1 +z} &= -\pi G_{3,3}^{2,2}\left( {z} \left|{\begin{array}{*{20}c} {0,0,1/2} \vspace{0.2cm}\\ {0,0,1/2} \end{array}} \right.\right) \\ \exp\left(-\alpha z\right) \Bessel{v}{ \alpha z} &= \sqrt{\pi} G_{1,2}^{2,0}\left({2\alpha z} \left|{\begin{array}{*{20}c} {1/2} \vspace{0.2cm}\\ {v,-v} \end{array}} \right. \right) \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Tabulated Meijer G forms for the logarithmic factor and the exponential-Bessel product.
nodes.section: 3 Average Sum-Rate of Distributed Alamouti Space-Time Codes with Two-Way AF Relaying

nodes.name: Meijer G-function as a special case of Fox's H-function
nodes.statement: \begin{align} G_{p,q}^{m,n}\left( {z} \left|{\begin{array}{*{20}c} {(a_p)} \vspace{0.2cm}\\ {(b_q)} \end{array}} \right.\right) = H_{p,q}^{m,n}\left( {z} \left|{\begin{array}{*{20}c} {(a_p,1)} \vspace{0.2cm}\\ {(b_q,1)} \end{array}} \right.\right) \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Every Meijer G equals a Fox H whose parameter pairs all carry unit second component.
nodes.section: 3 Average Sum-Rate of Distributed Alamouti Space-Time Codes with Two-Way AF Relaying

nodes.name: $I_1$ as an integral of a product of two Fox H-functions
nodes.statement: \begin{align} I_1 = - &\sum\limits_{u=1}^{2} \sum\limits_{v=0}^{1} \pi^{3/2} \mathcal{A}_v \int\limits_{0}^{\infty} z^u \exp\left[-\left(\beta_1 - \alpha\right)z\right] \nonumber \\ &\times H_{3,3}^{2,2}\left[ {z} \left|{\begin{array}{*{20}c} {(0,1),(0,1),(1/2,1)} \vspace{0.2cm}\\ {(0,1),(0,1),(1/2,1)} \end{array}} \right.\right] \nonumber \\ &\times H_{1,2}^{2,0}\left[{2\alpha z} \left|{\begin{array}{*{20}c} {(1/2,1)} \vspace{0.2cm}\\ {(v,1),(-v,1)} \end{array}} \right. \right] dz \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Substituting the H-function forms turns $I_1$ into a Laplace-type integral of a product of two Fox H-functions.
nodes.section: 3 Average Sum-Rate of Distributed Alamouti Space-Time Codes with Two-Way AF Relaying

nodes.name: Closed-form expression for $I_1$
nodes.statement: \begin{align} &I_1 = -\pi^{3/2} \sum\limits_{u=1}^{2} \sum\limits_{v=0}^{1} \mathcal{A}_v \left(\beta_1 - \alpha\right)^{-u-1} \nonumber \\ & H_{1,[3:1],0,[3:2]}^{1,2,0,2,2}\left[ {\begin{array}{*{20}c} \frac{1}{\alpha+\beta_1} \\ \\ \\ \frac{2\alpha}{\alpha+\beta_1} \\ \end{array}\left| {\begin{array}{*{20}c} (1+u,1) \\ (1/1,1);(0,1),(0,1),(1/2,1) \\ {\_}{\_} \\ (0,1),(0,1),(\tfrac{1}{2},1);(v,1),(-v,1) \\ \end{array}} \right.} \right] \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: $I_1$ evaluates in closed form as a double sum of generalized (two-variable) Fox H-functions.
nodes.section: 3 Average Sum-Rate of Distributed Alamouti Space-Time Codes with Two-Way AF Relaying

nodes.name: Integral representation of $I_3$
nodes.statement: \begin{align} I_3 = \sum\limits_{n=1}^2 \xi_n &\int\limits_{0}^{\infty} \ln\left(1+t\right) \left(t+\zeta\right)^{-3-n} \nonumber \\ &\times {_2}F_1\left(3+n,n+\tfrac{1}{2};\tfrac{7}{2};\tfrac{t+\eta}{t+\zeta}\right) dt \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: $I_3$ expressed as a sum of integrals of $\ln(1+t)$ against the Gauss-hypergeometric PDF of $T$.
nodes.section: 3 Average Sum-Rate of Distributed Alamouti Space-Time Codes with Two-Way AF Relaying

nodes.name: Meijer G-function representations of $\ln(1+\zeta x)$ and the Gauss hypergeometric factor

nodes.name: Approximated average sum-rate of two-way AF DASTC
nodes.statement: By substituting \eqref{eq:I:1:3} and $\eqref{eq:I:3:3}$ in \eqref{eq:SumRate:3} and considering the fact that $I_2$ can be obtained in a similar form of $I_1$, the sum-rate of DASTC with two-way AF relay can be shown as \begin{align} &\Rsum \approx -\frac{2\pi^{3/2}}{3\ln 2} \sum\limits_{k=1}^2 \sum\limits_{u=1}^{2} \sum\limits_{v=0}^{1} \mathcal{A}_v \left(\beta_k - \alpha\right)^{-u-1} \nonumber \\ & H_{1,[3:1],0,[3:2]}^{1,2,0,2,2}\left[ {\begin{array}{*{20}c} \frac{1}{\alpha+\beta_k} \\ \\ \\ \frac{2\alpha}{\alpha+\beta_k} \\ \end{array}\left| {\begin{array}{*{20}c} (1+u,1) \\ (1/1,1);(0,1),(0,1),(1/2,1) \\ {\_}{\_} \\ (0,1),(0,1),(\tfrac{1}{2},1);(v,1),(-v,1) \\ \end{array}} \right.} \right] \nonumber \\ &+ \frac{4}{3\ln2} \! \sum\limits_{n=1}^2 \xi_n H_{4,4}^{4,2} \! \left[{\zeta} \left|{\begin{array}{*{20}c} {(0,1),(2n,1),(1,1),(1,1)} \vspace{0.2cm}\\ {(2+n,1),(n-\tfrac{1}{2},1),(1,1),(0,1)} \end{array}} \right. \right] \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: High-SNR closed form: the two-way DASTC average sum-rate is a sum of generalized Fox H-functions plus $H_{4,4}^{4,2}$ terms.

nodes.name: PDF of the ratio $Z=\gamma_i\gamma_j/(\gamma_i+2\gamma_j)$
nodes.statement: Let $\snri{i}$ and $\snri{j}$ be statistically independent and not necessarily identically distributed (i.n.i.d.) exponential random variables with hazard rate $\snravei{i}$ and $\snravei{j}$, respectively. Suppose that the ratio of $Z$ takes the form \begin{align} Z=\frac{\snri{i} \snri{j}}{\snri{i} +2\snri{j}} \end{align} Then, we obtain the PDF of random variable $Z$ as \begin{align} \PDF{Z}{z} = \alpha z \exp\left(-\beta_i z\right) \left[\alpha\Bessel{0}{\alpha z} + \beta_i \Bessel{1}{\alpha z}\right] \end{align} where $\alpha = 2\sqrt{\frac{2}{\snravei{i}\snravei{j}}}$ and $\beta_i = \frac{1}{\snravei{j}} + \frac{2}{\snravei{i}}$.
nodes.statement_short: For i.n.i.d. exponential $\gamma_i,\gamma_j$, the ratio $Z$ has a Bessel-weighted exponential density.
nodes.section: Appendix Auxiliary Results
assumptions: Let $\snri{i}$ and $\snri{j}$ be statistically independent and not necessarily identically distributed (i.n.i.d.) exponential random variables with hazard rate $\snravei{i}$ and $\snravei{j}$, respectively
Suppose that the ratio of $Z$ takes the form \begin{align} Z=\frac{\snri{i} \snri{j}}{\snri{i} +2\snri{j}} \end{align}
conclusions: Then, we obtain the PDF of random variable $Z$ as \begin{align} \PDF{Z}{z} = \alpha z \exp\left(-\beta_i z\right) \left[\alpha\Bessel{0}{\alpha z} + \beta_i \Bessel{1}{\alpha z}\right] \end{align}

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 1
nodes.statement: Let us rewrite $Z$ in a more tractable form as \begin{align} Z = \left(X + Y\right)^{-1} \end{align} where $X=1/\snri{i}$ and $Y=2/\snri{j}$. Then, after some algebraic simplifications together with the help of \cite[eq.~(3.471.9)]{GR:00:Book}, the moment generating function (MGF) of $X$ and $Y$ can be expressed as, respectively \begin{align} &\MGF{X}{s} = \EXs{X}{\exp\left(-s x\right)} = 2 \sqrt{\frac{s}{\snravei{i}}} \Bessel{1}{2 \sqrt{\frac{s}{\snravei{i}}}} \\ &\MGF{Y}{s} = \EXs{Y}{\exp\left(-s y\right)} = 2 \sqrt{\frac{2s}{\snravei{j}}} \Bessel{1}{2 \sqrt{\frac{2s}{\snravei{j}}}} \end{align} As can be seen from \eqref{eq:Z}, since $1/Z$ is the sum of two statistically independent random variables, by using \eqref{eq:MGF:X} and \eqref{eq:MGF:Y}, the MGF of $1/Z$ can be expressed as \begin{align} \MGF{1/Z}{s} = 4\sqrt{\frac{2}{\snravei{i}\snravei{j}}}s \Bessel{1}{2 \sqrt{\frac{s}{\snravei{i}}}} \Bessel{1}{2 \sqrt{\frac{2s}{\snravei{j}}}} \end{align} Then, the cumulative distribution function (CDF) of $1/Z$, $\CDF{1/Z}{x}$, can be shown as \begin{eqnarray} \CDF{1/Z}{x} =1- \mathcal{L}^{-1}\{\MGF{1/Z}{s}/s\}|_{1/x} \end{eqnarray} where $\mathcal{L}^{-1}\{.\}$ stands for the inverse Laplace transform. From \eqref{eq:MGF:1:Z} and \eqref{eq:CDF:1:Z} together with \cite[eq.~(13.2.20)]{RK:66:Book}, we have \begin{align} \CDF{Z}{z} = 1 - \alpha z \exp\left(-\beta_i z\right) \Bessel{1}{\alpha z} \end{align} where $\alpha = 2\sqrt{\frac{2}{\snravei{i}\snravei{j}}}$ and $\beta_i = \frac{1}{\snravei{j}} + \frac{2}{\snravei{i}}$. By differentiating \eqref{eq:CDF:Z:1} with respect to $z$ and using the fact that $\tfrac{d\Bessel{v}{z}}{dz}=-\Bessel{v-1}{z}-\tfrac{v}{z}\Bessel{v}{z}$ \cite[eq.~(8.486.12)]{GR:00:Book}, we obtain \eqref{eq:PDF:Z:1} which completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Write $1/Z=X+Y$, multiply the MGFs of $X$ and $Y$, invert the Laplace transform to get the CDF, then differentiate.

nodes.name: Rewrite $Z$ as the inverse of a sum

nodes.name: MGFs of $X$ and $Y$
nodes.statement: Then, after some algebraic simplifications together with the help of \cite[eq.~(3.471.9)]{GR:00:Book}, the moment generating function (MGF) of $X$ and $Y$ can be expressed as, respectively \begin{align} &\MGF{X}{s} = \EXs{X}{\exp\left(-s x\right)} = 2 \sqrt{\frac{s}{\snravei{i}}} \Bessel{1}{2 \sqrt{\frac{s}{\snravei{i}}}} \\ &\MGF{Y}{s} = \EXs{Y}{\exp\left(-s y\right)} = 2 \sqrt{\frac{2s}{\snravei{j}}} \Bessel{1}{2 \sqrt{\frac{2s}{\snravei{j}}}} \end{align}

nodes.name: MGF of $1/Z$ by independence
nodes.statement: As can be seen from \eqref{eq:Z}, since $1/Z$ is the sum of two statistically independent random variables, by using \eqref{eq:MGF:X} and \eqref{eq:MGF:Y}, the MGF of $1/Z$ can be expressed as \begin{align} \MGF{1/Z}{s} = 4\sqrt{\frac{2}{\snravei{i}\snravei{j}}}s \Bessel{1}{2 \sqrt{\frac{s}{\snravei{i}}}} \Bessel{1}{2 \sqrt{\frac{2s}{\snravei{j}}}} \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Multiply the two MGFs, since $1/Z$ is a sum of independent variables.

nodes.name: CDF of $1/Z$ via inverse Laplace transform
nodes.statement: Then, the cumulative distribution function (CDF) of $1/Z$, $\CDF{1/Z}{x}$, can be shown as \begin{eqnarray} \CDF{1/Z}{x} =1- \mathcal{L}^{-1}\{\MGF{1/Z}{s}/s\}|_{1/x} \end{eqnarray} where $\mathcal{L}^{-1}\{.\}$ stands for the inverse Laplace transform.
nodes.statement_short: Express the CDF of $1/Z$ as one minus the inverse Laplace transform of $\Phi_{1/Z}(s)/s$.

nodes.name: Closed-form CDF of $Z$
nodes.statement: From \eqref{eq:MGF:1:Z} and \eqref{eq:CDF:1:Z} together with \cite[eq.~(13.2.20)]{RK:66:Book}, we have \begin{align} \CDF{Z}{z} = 1 - \alpha z \exp\left(-\beta_i z\right) \Bessel{1}{\alpha z} \end{align} where $\alpha = 2\sqrt{\frac{2}{\snravei{i}\snravei{j}}}$ and $\beta_i = \frac{1}{\snravei{j}} + \frac{2}{\snravei{i}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Invert the transform using a tabulated pair to obtain $F_Z(z)=1-\alpha z e^{-\beta_i z}\mathcal{K}_1(\alpha z)$.

nodes.name: Differentiate the CDF to obtain the PDF
nodes.statement: By differentiating \eqref{eq:CDF:Z:1} with respect to $z$ and using the fact that $\tfrac{d\Bessel{v}{z}}{dz}=-\Bessel{v-1}{z}-\tfrac{v}{z}\Bessel{v}{z}$ \cite[eq.~(8.486.12)]{GR:00:Book}, we obtain \eqref{eq:PDF:Z:1} which completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate the CDF using the $\mathcal{K}_v$ derivative recurrence to reach the claimed density.

nodes.name: PDF of $T=\gamma_0(\gamma_1+\gamma_2)/(\gamma_1\gamma_2)$
nodes.statement: Let $\snri{0}$, $\snri{1}$, and $\snri{2}$ be the three i.n.i.d. exponential random variables with hazard rates $\snravei{0}$, $\snravei{1}$, and $\snravei{2}$, respectively, then the PDF of $T=\snri{0}\frac{\snri{1}+\snri{2}}{\snri{1}\snri{2}}$ is given by \begin{align} \PDF{T}{t} = \! \! \sum\limits_{n=1}^2 \xi_n \tfrac{1}{(t+\zeta)^{3+n}} {_2}F_1\left(3+n,n+\tfrac{1}{2};\tfrac{7}{2};\tfrac{t+\eta}{t+\zeta}\right) \end{align} where \begin{align*} \xi_n &= \sqrt{\pi} \left(\frac{4}{\sqrt{\snravei{1}\snravei{2}}}\right)^{n} \frac{\Gamma\left(3+n\right)\Gamma\left(3-n\right)}{\Gamma\left(7/2\right)} \varpi_n \nonumber \\ \varpi_0 &= \frac{4}{\snravei{0}\snravei{1}\snravei{2}}, \hspace{0.5cm} \varpi_1 = \frac{2\left(\snravei{1}+\snravei{2}\right)}{\snravei{0}\left(\snravei{1}\snravei{2}\right)^{3/2}} \nonumber \\ \zeta &= \snravei{0} \left(\frac{1}{\snravei{1}} + \frac{1}{\snravei{2}} + \frac{2}{\snravei{1}\snravei{2}}\right), \hspace{0.3cm} \eta = \snravei{0} \left(\frac{1}{\snravei{1}} + \frac{1}{\snravei{2}} - \frac{2}{\snravei{1}\snravei{2}}\right) \end{align*} and $_2F_1\left(a,b;c;z\right)$ is the Gauss hypergeometric function \cite[eq.~(2.12.1)]{Erd:53:Book}.
nodes.statement_short: For three i.n.i.d. exponentials, $T$ has a two-term Gauss-hypergeometric density with explicit constants $\xi_n,\zeta,\eta$.

nodes.statement: Since $T=\snri{0}\frac{\snri{1}+\snri{2}}{\snri{1}\snri{2}}$, by defining $W=\frac{\snri{1}\snri{2}}{\snri{1}+\snri{2}}$, we have \begin{align} \CDF{T}{t} = \int\nolimits_{0}^{\infty} \left[1-\exp\left(-\frac{wt}{\snravei{0}}\right)\right] \PDF{W}{w} dw \end{align}

nodes.statement: Following similar steps as in Lemma~\ref{lemma:1}, we obtain $\PDF{W}{w}$ as \begin{align} &\PDF{W}{w} = \frac{2w}{\snravei{1}\snravei{2}} \exp\left[-\left(\frac{1}{\snravei{1}}+\frac{1}{\snravei{2}}\right)w\right] \nonumber \\ &\times \left[ 2\Bessel{0}{\frac{2w}{\sqrt{\snravei{1}\snravei{2}}}} + \left(\frac{\snravei{1}+\snravei{2}}{\snravei{1}\snravei{2}}\right) \Bessel{1}{\frac{2w}{\sqrt{\snravei{1}\snravei{2}}}} \right] \end{align}

nodes.statement: In the first example, we consider the symmetric relaying protocol, i.e., $\CP{0}=\CP{1}=\CP{2}=1$.

nodes.name: Example 2 — co-linear relay geometry
nodes.statement: In the second example, we assume that the geometry for locations of three communicating terminals is co-linear where the relay is placed half way between the two sources, i.e., $\CP{1}=\CP{2}=16$ and $\CP{0}=1$.
nodes.statement_short: Relay placed midway between the sources on a line, giving $\Omega_1=\Omega_2=16$, $\Omega_0=1$.

nodes.name: Tightness of the analytical approximation
nodes.statement: As can be observed from these two figures, the analysis is very tight from the middle to high SNR regime. Specifically, from SNR=10 dB the analytical and simulation curves perfectly match with each other which verify the tightness of our approximation.
nodes.section: 4 Numerical Results

nodes.name: Spectral-efficiency gain over one-way DASTC
nodes.statement: More importantly, the proposed two-way DASTC scheme outperforms the conventional one-way system in terms of the spectral efficiency in the whole considered range of SNR. In particular, at SNR=30 dB, the proposed scheme enhances the average sum-rate to 3.8 bps/Hz in both Example 1 and 2 compared to the conventional one.
nodes.statement_short: The two-way scheme beats one-way DASTC at every SNR, gaining 3.8 bps/Hz at 30 dB in both examples.
nodes.section: 4 Numerical Results

nodes.name: Gain is independent of relay location
nodes.statement: It is interesting to observe that with a fixed value of $\CP{0}$ the gain is unchanged, irrespective of the relay's location.
